stem.text: Let g and h be continuous functions with \( \int_{-2}^{3} g(x)\,dx = 5 \), \( \int_{0}^{3} g(x)\,dx = -4 \), and \( \int_{0}^{-2} h(x)\,dx = 1 \). Find the value of \( \int_{-2}^{0} \left(-3g(x) + 2h(x)\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the given integral of h: \( \int_{-2}^{0} h(x)\,dx = -(1) = -1 \), and use linearity on the requested integral.

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, one supplied integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: a linear combination of two functions

distractor_derivations.B: given integral of h from 0 to -2 used as if it ran from -2 to 0
distractor_derivations.C: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral of g from -2 to 0 as -4 - (5)
distractor_derivations.D: integral of g from 3 to 0 taken as -4 instead of 4
